data.content_ref: inline:{"analogy":null,"claim":"A decentralized network of small services is more resilient than a single large service because independent failure modes do not share common triggers, limiting systemic correlation.","counterconditions":[{"case":"If operators adopt identical cloud infrastructure or standardized auto-scaling algorithms, hidden correlations emerge that synchronize failures.","checker_spec":null,"eval":"observation"},{"case":"If a shared external dependency (e.g., a major cloud provider or CDN) fails, both the large service and the decentralized network fail in correlation.","checker_spec":null,"eval":"observation"}],"definitions":[],"derivation":[],"formalization_refs":[],"mechanism":"Independently operated services possess distinct administrative domains, deployment schedules, and software stacks, creating a 'defense in depth' where local failures remain localized and do not propagate system-wide.","premises":[],"schema":"deepreason-reasoning-envelope-v1","scope":{"covers":[],"excludes":[]},"simulation_refs":[],"uncertainties":[]}
